currentCard.prompt: Какая трубка проводит мочу от почки к мочевому пузырю?

answers.note: Уретра — трубка у выхода из мочевого пузыря; по ней моча покидает организм при мочеиспускании.
У человека два мочеточника — тонкие мышечные трубки, соединяющие каждую почку с мочевым пузырём.
Почечная артерия несёт кровь в почку и разветвляется на более мелкие сосуды.
Собирательные протоки проводят образованную нефронами мочу к чашечкам почки.

currentCard.explanation: Мочеточники — тонкие мышечные трубки, соединяющие почки с мочевым пузырём и проводящие туда мочу. Поэтому правильный ответ — мочеточник.

source.title: The Urinary Tract & How It Works — NIDDK

literal.prompt: Какая трубка проводит мочу от почки к мочевому пузырю?

sixLiteralCanonicalGroups.individualGround: NIDDK Urinary Tract L216 explicitly identifies ureters as muscular tubes connecting kidneys and bladder and carrying urine to the bladder. L219 puts urethra downstream of the bladder. OpenStax L43 puts collecting ducts upstream, within the kidney leading to calyces; L47 then directs urine from pelvis into ureter. NIDDK Kidneys L193 assigns incoming blood, not urine, to the renal artery. The endpoint-defined route therefore has only key1. All four labels name anatomical conduits associated with renal/urinary function, with credible ureter/urethra and collecting-duct confusions.

sixLiteralCanonicalGroups.literal: Мочеточники — тонкие мышечные трубки, соединяющие почки с мочевым пузырём и проводящие туда мочу. Поэтому правильный ответ — мочеточник.
sixLiteralCanonicalGroups.individualGround: Both sentences are true: NIDDK Urinary Tract L216 supplies thin muscular tubes, kidney-to-bladder connection and urine transport. The second directly names мочеточник as the answer. Plural anatomical definition followed by singular answer is coherent; two sentences and within length limit.

sixLiteralCanonicalGroups.literal: Уретра — трубка у выхода из мочевого пузыря; по ней моча покидает организм при мочеиспускании.
sixLiteralCanonicalGroups.individualGround: NIDDK Urinary Tract L219 places the urethra at the bottom of the bladder and states that urine exits the body through it during urination. «у выхода» is a natural description of that location. The note teaches this distractor’s own downstream route rather than assigning it ureter function.

sixLiteralCanonicalGroups.literal: У человека два мочеточника — тонкие мышечные трубки, соединяющие каждую почку с мочевым пузырём.
sixLiteralCanonicalGroups.individualGround: NIDDK Urinary Tract L213 gives two ureters, and L216 describes thin muscular tubes linking kidneys to bladder. NIDDK Kidneys L167 explicitly places one ureter on each side. The note therefore adds number (two), thinness and muscular construction beyond the prompt/key connection and conveys the paired relationship without inventing it.

sixLiteralCanonicalGroups.literal: Почечная артерия несёт кровь в почку и разветвляется на более мелкие сосуды.
sixLiteralCanonicalGroups.individualGround: NIDDK Kidneys L193 explicitly says blood enters the kidney through the renal artery, which branches into smaller vessels until reaching nephrons. OpenStax L48/L51 independently describes the renal artery and its successive branching. This is an incoming blood-vessel fact about its own option, not a urine conduit claim.

sixLiteralCanonicalGroups.literal: Собирательные протоки проводят образованную нефронами мочу к чашечкам почки.
sixLiteralCanonicalGroups.individualGround: OpenStax L43 explicitly states that collecting ducts transport urine made by nephrons to kidney calyces. The note retains that internal destination rather than saying a collecting duct runs directly from kidney to bladder. It is a substantive own-option fact.

absoluteLevel.assessment: Distinguishing ureter from urethra and an intrarenal collecting duct requires thematic familiarity with human urinary anatomy. The general adult may know kidneys produce urine without knowing the exact connecting tube. Two close urinary alternatives remain plausible even after excluding the blood vessel. This is introductory anatomy rather than a specialist detail or hard multistep inference.

correctNoteExtraFact.fact: Humans ordinarily have two ureters; they are thin muscular tubes, with each kidney connected to the bladder. Number and muscular construction go beyond identifying the route in the prompt.
